examples.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$. Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+0\cdot 5+1\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,-1,-4⟩$ and $b=⟨6,-5,3⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 6+(-1)\cdot (-5)+(-4)\cdot 3}{{6}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{19}{70}⟨6,-5,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{57}{35},\frac{19}{14},-\frac{57}{70}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
